notes_list.title: Rules to Decide Conclusions
notes_list.basic_overview: Treat the statement as true even if it differs from common facts. Check whether the conclusion can be proved 100% using only the statement.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Scope-stretching words (any, all, every, each, never, always, only) are red flags. Qualifying words (many, some, often, usually, can, may) are safer and more likely to follow.

notes_list.title: Example: Problem Solving
notes_list.basic_overview: Statement: The best way to deal with a problem is to solve it. I: Solving any problem is easy. II: Solving a problem is better than ignoring it.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Conclusion I fails because of 'any' and 'easy' (not stated). Conclusion II follows. Answer: only conclusion II follows.

notes_list.title: Angle between Clock Hands
notes_list.basic_overview: Angle = | 30H - (11/2) M |, where the time is H hours M minutes. If the result exceeds 180 degrees, subtract it from 360.

notes_list.title: Day Code Method
notes_list.basic_overview: Add: date, month code, century code, number of leap years in the year digits (yy divided by 4), and yy; take the sum modulo 7. Codes: 1=Sun, 2=Mon, 3=Tue, 4=Wed, 5=Thu, 6=Fri, 0=Sat.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Month codes: Jan 1, Feb 4, Mar 4, Apr 0, May 2, Jun 5, Jul 0, Aug 3, Sep 6, Oct 1, Nov 4, Dec 6. Century: 2000s = 6. In a leap year, subtract 1 for January and February. Example 14 March 2026: 0+4+6+6+5 = 21, so Saturday. Practice: 19 November 2032 = Friday.

topics.topic_title: Painted Cube Cut into n^3 Cubes

notes_list.title: Painted Cube Formulas
notes_list.basic_overview: For an n x n x n cube painted on all faces: no colour (n-2)^3; one face 6(n-2)^2; two faces 12(n-2); three faces 8.
